A FEW THINGS TO KNOW

Good questions.
Clear answers.

What is a corporate bond?

A corporate bond is debt issued by a company to raise money. Unlike a share, it does not represent equity ownership. Its terms define interest payments and repayment at maturity.

Why do bond prices move?

Prices respond to interest-rate expectations, economic news, the issuer’s financial health and market liquidity. Different bonds can react differently to the same event.

What does fractional bond trading mean?

Fractional sizing lets traders take smaller positions rather than purchasing a whole conventional bond denomination. Minimum trade sizes depend on the instrument and trading venue.

Which bonds can my audience trade?

The current focus is corporate bonds from familiar companies. The available instrument list varies by venue. Government bonds are planned and should not be assumed available.

Can traders go long, short and use leverage?

Long/short trading and leverage are available subject to the venue and instrument terms. Leverage increases both potential gains and losses; trading hours and limits should be checked on the chosen venue.

Do I need to be a bond expert?

No. We can help you get started with training materials and a product walkthrough, so you can build your understanding and introduce the market confidently and accurately.

Will BondTrader provide marketing and content support?

Yes. BondTrader will provide training materials and ideas for content creators, supported by product walkthroughs and approved marketing assets. We are also developing a branded bond guide for partners.

What are builder fees, and how do I earn them?

Builder fees are volume-based partner remuneration—familiar to FX/CFD affiliates and IBs as commissions or rebates. Earn from qualifying referred trading activity, with your agreement setting out the applicable terms, eligible volume and payment arrangements.

Where will my referred customers trade?

BondTrader connects customers to supported trading venues, including the Web3 venue BondSwap and participating brokers such as Navion and BLKBOX. Availability depends on the customer’s jurisdiction and chosen venue.

Can I promote multiple programmes or introduce an IB network?

Yes, subject to agreement. Partnerships can cover multiple campaigns, and tailored arrangements can support IBs and larger networks. Each programme uses its assigned tracking links and applicable terms.
